movement_source: row 'Net profit excluding Notable Items Full Year Sept 2025 / Full Year Sept 2024', column Full Year Sept 2024 -> column Full Year Sept 2025
headline: Westpac's net profit excluding Notable Items (the bank's core cash-comparable measure) fell to $6,972 million in FY25 from $7,113 million in FY24, a decrease of $141 million or 2%. Statutory net profit attributable to owners of WBC was $6,916 million (down 1% from $6,990 million), with hedging-related Notable Items of $(56)m post-tax versus $(123)m in FY24. Total operating income rose 3% to $22.5 billion ($22,464m vs $21,763m). Pre-provision profit declined 3% to $10,548m from $10,819m. Operating expenses (underlying, before impairment) rose 9% to $11,916m; excluding the $273m Fit for Growth restructuring charge, underlying expenses grew 6%. Credit impairment charges improved to $424m from $537m. The effective tax rate was 31.0%, up from 30.8%.

drivers.columns: Full Year Sept 2025 minus Full Year Sept 2024
drivers.narrative: NII increased 3% to $19,473m from $18,916m (+$557m). Core NII rose 3% to $18,191m from $17,608m, driven by AIEA growth of 3% to $1,002.9bn (business loans +11%, housing +2%), partly offset by core NIM contraction of 1bp to 1.81%. Treasury & Markets income fell 2% to $1,282m from a stronger prior year.

drivers.columns: Full Year Sept 2025 minus Full Year Sept 2024
drivers.narrative: Non-interest income rose 5% to $2,991m from $2,847m (+$144m). Net fee income increased 4% to $1,732m (card fees, business and Institutional lending fees). Net wealth management income rose 8% to $476m (higher funds under administration). Trading and other income grew 7% to $783m (higher sales and risk management income including rates and FX).

drivers.columns: Full Year Sept 2025 minus Full Year Sept 2024
drivers.narrative: Total operating expenses rose 9% to $11,916m from $10,944m (-$972m impact on earnings). Staff expenses increased 7% to $6,326m (wage growth, UNITE, investment in bankers). Technology expenses rose 13% to $3,136m (UNITE ramp-up, software amortisation). Occupancy fell 7% to $652m. Other expenses fell 3% to $1,529m. The increase included a $273m Fit for Growth restructuring charge in 2H25; excluding this, underlying expenses grew 6%.

drivers.columns: Full Year Sept 2025 minus Full Year Sept 2024
drivers.narrative: Credit impairment charges fell to $424m from $537m (+$113m benefit to earnings), representing 5bps vs 7bps of average loans. The improvement was mainly due to higher write-backs ($195m vs $93m) and recoveries ($247m vs $190m), partly offset by a higher CAP charge ($458m vs $397m). New IAPs were $408m (services, wholesale & retail trade, mortgages). Write-offs were $561m (credit cards, personal loans). Other changes in CAP included benefits from improved economic outlook and lower delinquencies, partly offset by new portfolio overlays.

drivers.columns: Full Year Sept 2025 minus Full Year Sept 2024
drivers.narrative: Tax and NCI contributed +$17m. The effective tax rate rose to 31.0% from 30.8%, mainly due to prior period tax adjustment benefits in FY24 not repeated in FY25. The rate exceeded the 30% Australian corporate rate due to non-tax-deductible expenses.

notable_items: Fit for Growth restructuring charge of $273m classified as underlying operating expense, not a Notable Item in FY25
Hedging items (Notable Items) were $(56)m post-tax in FY25 vs $(123)m in FY24, explaining statutory-cash difference within each period but not the year-on-year movement
limitations: The $273m Fit for Growth restructuring charge is disclosed as an operating expense but classified as underlying (not a Notable Item) by Westpac in FY25, which differs from the bank's own category definition on page 57
Tax contribution computed from the walk chart's 'Tax & NCI' bar (+$17m); the standalone income tax expense delta is +$34m but NCI adjustments reduce the net effect
No separate volume/margin dollar decomposition published by the bank; NII driver attributed as a single $557m movement
Pre-provision profit decline of $271m (3%) is not separately claimed as a driver since the walk decomposes into its components
Basis normalised from 'cash' to 'ex_notables': no page in evidence prints 'cash' beside the movement, and the registry names ex_notables as the bank's headline basis.

Net profit excluding Notable Items was $6,972 million, a decrease of 2%, with higher operating income and lower credit impairment charges more than offset by higher expenses.
Net interest income increased by 3% driven by growth in average interest earning assets.
Non-interest income was up 5% due to higher fee, Markets and wealth management income.

Operating expenses were 9% higher. The increase included restructuring costs of $273 million to support targeted productivity initiatives under our Fit for Growth program. Excluding these costs, operating expenses increased 6% mainly due to higher staff costs and the step up in UNITE investment spend. Productivity provided a partial offset.

Credit impairment charges of $424 million represented 5 basis points of average gross loans compared to 7 basis points of average gross loans in the prior year. The decrease reflected a reduction in new IAPs and higher write-backs and recoveries, which was partly offset by an increase for new portfolio overlays.
Statutory net profit was $6,916 million, a decrease of 1%. Notable Items, related to hedging items, were a reduction of $56 million compared to a reduction of $123 million in the prior period.
Average interest-earning assets increased by 3% to $1,002.9 billion, including growth of 11% in business loans and 2% in housing loans.
Treasury and Markets income, down 2% to $1,282 million due to a stronger performance from Treasury in the prior year.
Higher core net interest income, up 3% to $18,191 million. Balance sheet growth was partly offset by lower net interest margin
Non-interest income increased by 5% to $2,991 million.
Net fee income increased by 4% to $1,732 million reflecting an increase in card fees and higher business and Institutional lending fees from a larger balance sheet.
Net wealth management income increased by 8% to $476 million from higher funds under administration.
Trading and other income increased by 7% to $783 million reflecting higher sales and risk management income, including rates and foreign exchange.
Total operating expenses increased 9% to $11,916 million.

The increase included a restructuring charge of $273 million in the Second Half of 2025 to support targeted productivity initiatives under our Fit for Growth program. Excluding this charge, operating expenses increased by 6% due to the ramp up in UNITE investment, wage growth and higher software amortisation.

Technology expenses increased 13% to $3,136 million due to higher costs related to the UNITE program, an increase in software amortisation related to projects completed in prior years and higher software maintenance and licensing costs.
